newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 15.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 15.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
** Indian scooter and motorcycle maker Bajaj Auto on Wednesday announced sluggish growth for the financial year ended March 31 due to an industrial slowdown that hit vehicle sales during the period.
Bajaj Auto -- among the world's largest makers of two- and three-wheelers -- announced a modest five percent rise in net profit to 4.40 billion rupees, from 4.18 billion in 1995/96.
The firm's net profit had surged nearly 40 percent in 1995/96 from the previous year.
** Bajaj shares ended 68.75 rupees, or eight percent up at 918.50 at the Bombay exchange despite the sluggish results.
Traders said the stock surged after the firm said its board would meet on Monday to announce a bonus issue of equity shares.
But the firm's chairman said after trading hours he was not in favour of issuing a bonus in the proportion of one share for every share held.

** Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd is gearing up to raise 10 billion rupees through short and long term debt instruments to fund financial requirements of cash-strapped public sector undertakings through borrowed funds, the Financial Express daily reports.
** Engineering firm, Thermax Ltd on Wednesday posted a four percent fall in 1996/97 (april-March). Shares of Thermax ended 8.0 rupees higher at 286.0.
** The Indian rupee opened Thursday at 35.82/825 per dollar, unchanged from Wednesday's close, dealers said.
Quiet trade seen during the day, with the rupee in a 35.80-35.83 range, dealers said.
** Indian shares rallied smartly to close higher on Wednesday, buoyed by an announcement of a bonus issue by scootermaker Bajaj Auto, traders said.
** Bombay's benchmark share index closed 38.57 points, or 1.04 percent up at 3,740.53.
** Zee Telefilms is due to announce results, for the year ended March 31, 1997, later on Wednesday.
